Definition: a member of a flock, i.e. a sheep or goat
BiblicalUsage: A seh is a sheep or a goat of the flock, and it stands at the centre of the Passover. Every man shall take a lamb according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for a house, and if the household be too little for the lamb, let him and his neighbour take it together. The same word is the clean beast for the table, and the sheep Saul commanded the people to bring and slay without sinning against the LORD in eating with the blood.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lamb for a house is the heart of the whole Bible in one small word: one lamb, one house, and the blood on the doorposts. Every later lamb — and the Lamb — stands in this one's place. And I hold that the counting by souls, every man according to his eating, says the sacrifice is measured to the need, and the need is met exactly.
